carousels.name: 5 excuses partners hear about p*rn, and what they really mean

slides.title: "I watch p*rn for your safety." [[5 excuses partners hear — decoded.]]
slides.sub: If you've heard one of these, read till the end.

slides.title: "It's for [[your]] safety."
slides.body: Turning a partner's boundary into the reason for p*rn shifts the blame onto them. Nobody's safety requires secret accounts.

slides.title: "It's [[private]]. It has nothing to do with you."
slides.body: In a relationship, something that affects trust, intimacy and time together isn't fully private. Privacy is fine. Secrecy that hurts someone isn't.

slides.title: Excuses [[3–5]]
items: "Every guy watches p*rn." — Common isn't the same as harmless.
"I can stop whenever." — Then the question is why he hasn't.
"You're overreacting." — Feelings about broken trust aren't overreacting.

slides.title: The real red flag [[isn't]] the p*rn.
slides.body: On the biggest Reddit threads about this, people kept saying the same thing: the struggle is one thing — getting defensive and dismissive when asked is another.

slides.title: 8 things your partner feels [[when she finds your p*rn.]]
slides.sub: What partners say on the threads men never read.

slides.title: Feelings [[1–4]]
items: "Am I not enough?" — comparing herself to a screen.
Betrayed — more by the hiding than the p*rn.
Confused — "he says he loves me, so why?"
Embarrassed to tell anyone.

slides.title: Feelings [[5–8]]
items: Watched — wondering what he thinks of real women now.
Lonely — he's there, but not really present.
Guilty for even being upset.
Hopeful — if he's honest and actually changes.

slides.title: Her feelings are [[valid]].
slides.body: You don't have to agree with every reaction. But brushing them off is how trust breaks completely. Listen before you defend.

Show a plan to quit p*rn, not just promises.

Get support — together or separately.

carousels.name: Years in, years out: 7 lessons from men who quit p*rn

slides.title: 15 years addicted. 5 years free. [[7 lessons men who quit p*rn keep repeating.]]
slides.sub: Pulled from recovery stories that went viral on Reddit.

slides.title: Lessons [[1–3]]
items: The lying hurt more than the p*rn. Many say relationships ended over the hiding, not the habit.
Denial is the longest phase. "It's not p*rn causing this" can last years.
Symptoms show up everywhere — anxiety, brain fog, bad sleep, low confidence.

slides.title: Lessons [[4–5]]
items: Hiding keeps p*rn alive. Telling one person is often the turning point.
Shame doesn't heal you. Grace and forgiveness do — for yourself too.

slides.title: Lessons [[6–7]]
items: Quitting p*rn takes time. Months, not days — with setbacks.
Life after is real. Many describe deeper relationships, more confidence, work they're proud of.

slides.title: You can [[skip]] the 15 years.
slides.body: Every lesson above was learned the hard way. You can start using them tonight.
